title: Higher-Call Prime-Power Survival Closed Forms: Eisenstein Isomorphism, Simplex Injectivity, Squared-Trinomial Zero Law, and Fourier Eigenvalue Spectra

theorems.name: Unimodular Eisenstein Isomorphism and Squared-Trinomial Zero-Difference Law
theorems.statement: The unimodular Z-linear map iota(x, y) = (x + y) + y*omega from Z^2 to Z[omega] (omega = e^(2*pi*i/3)) maps beta_0 = (1, 0), beta_1 = (-1, 1), beta_2 = (0, -1) to 1, omega, omega^2. At any fixed call count k >= 1, the map (a, b, c) -> (a - b, b - c) is strictly injective on the simplex Sigma_k = {(a, b, c) in Z_(>=0)^3 : a + b + c = k}, so the number of distinct integer endpoints is (k + 1)*(k + 2)/2 and the exact number of ordered path pairs with Delta(t, u) = (0, 0) in Z^2 is N_k(0) = sum_(a+b+c=k) (k! / (a! b! c!))^2.

theorems.name: Histogram Congruence Criterion for 3^h | Delta(t, u)
theorems.statement: For any two k-call paths with digit histograms (a, b, c), (a', b', c') in Sigma_k and differences delta_a = a - a', delta_b = b - b', delta_c = c - c' (delta_a + delta_b + delta_c = 0), 3^h divides Delta(t, u) = (delta_a - delta_b, delta_b - delta_c) if and only if delta_a === delta_b === delta_c === r * 3^(h - 1) (mod 3^h) for some r in {0, 1, 2}.

theorems.name: Exact Fourier Eigenvalue Formula for Prime-Power Survival N_k(3^h)
theorems.statement: For every h >= 1 and k >= 1, the prime-power survival count N_k(3^h) = |{(t, u) : 3^h | Delta(t, u)}| equals (1 / 9^h) * sum_(u, v in Z_(3^h)^2) Lambda_h(u, v)^k, where Lambda_h(u, v) = 3 + 2*cos(2*pi*(2u - v)/3^h) + 2*cos(2*pi*(u + v)/3^h) + 2*cos(2*pi*(u - 2v)/3^h).
